```{r setup}
library(lumen)
```

## The pipeline

```
 source ──► ingest_adam() ──► validate_adam() ──► preprocess_adam() ──► cache ──► app
 (raw ADaM)   read raw data     data contract       analysis datasets    memory + disk
```

`load_lumen_data()` runs the pipeline and returns the 13 analysis-ready
datasets, from cache whenever possible.

## Three data sources

### Bundled (default)

The pre-generated synthetic datasets shipped with *random.cdisc.data*
(`cadsl`, `cadae`, ...). Fast, and always the same data.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
raw <- ingest_adam("bundled")
```

### Freshly generated synthetic data

Generated with the `random.cdisc.data::rad*()` functions. Choose the number
of subjects and the seed; extra arguments can be passed to each generator.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
raw <- ingest_adam(
  "synthetic",
  synthetic = list(
    N = 200,                                  # subjects
    seed = 7,                                 # change for a new draw
    args = list(ADAE = list(max_n_aes = 5))   # per-dataset rad*() arguments
  )
)
```

With `seed = NA` a random seed is drawn once per session, printed in the
console and stored in option `lumen.synthetic`, so the app and its "Show R
code" always use the same draw.

### Parquet files

Point `parquet_dir` at a folder with one file per dataset: `adsl.parquet`,
`adae.parquet`, ... (or `adsl_adam.parquet`, ...; case-insensitive). Other files
are ignored; extra ADaM datasets are read but reported as unused. Needs the
*arrow* package.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
raw <- ingest_adam("parquet", parquet_dir = "path/to/adam")
```

`export_adam_parquet()` writes data in that layout, e.g. to freeze a synthetic
draw:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
export_adam_parquet(ingest_adam("synthetic", list(N = 200, seed = 7)), "cache")
run_app(source = "parquet", parquet_dir = "cache")
```

## The data contract

Every source is checked right after ingestion, so data problems are reported
before the app starts instead of failing inside a module. The contract lists
the datasets and columns the app needs:

```{r}
names(adam_contract())
adam_contract()$ADTTE
```

`validate_adam()` stops with the full list of problems (missing datasets or
columns, empty datasets, an ADSL with more than one row per subject) and
warns about subjects that have no ADSL record.

The app's modules also pre-select some values (e.g. the overall survival
parameter `OS`). With real data these may not exist; `check_app_defaults()`
warns about each missing one, so you know which defaults to adjust:

```{r}
adam_app_defaults()[[1]]
```

## Readable adverse event names

*random.cdisc.data* codes the adverse event hierarchy with placeholders
(`"dcd A.1.1.1.1"`). Pre-processing replaces them with illustrative
MedDRA-style names; the mapping is one-to-one per level, so no AE groups are
merged and all counts are unchanged. Real MedDRA terms pass through untouched.

```{r}
head(ae_dictionary(), 4)
decode_ae_terms(data.frame(AEDECOD = c("dcd A.1.1.1.1", "dcd D.1.1.4.2", "Headache")))
```

## Caching

`load_lumen_data()` uses the first valid cache:

1. **session memory** - instant for repeated launches in one R session;
2. **disk** - `lumen_adam.rds` in `tools::R_user_dir("lumen", "cache")`
   (option `lumen.cache_dir`);
3. **fresh build** - then cached.

The cache is rebuilt automatically when the package version or any
data-producing function changes, or when the source changes (source type,
synthetic settings, *random.cdisc.data* version, or a parquet file's name,
size or modification time). Force a rebuild with `refresh = TRUE` (option
`lumen.refresh_cache`) or clear everything with `lumen_clear_cache()`.

## Switching to real study data

1. Export the ADaM datasets as parquet (`adsl.parquet`, ...) into one folder.
2. `run_app(source = "parquet", parquet_dir = "that/folder")`.
3. Fix anything `validate_adam()` reports; review the warnings of
   `check_app_defaults()` and adjust the module defaults if needed.
4. Run the test suite (`devtools::test()`); the data invariants run on every
   data scenario (see `vignette("development", package = "lumen")`).
